###Chapter 1
Chapter 1:
At night, the spacious living room glowed under bright lights as two people sat across from each other, a divorce agreement resting between them.
Kristian Shaw, impeccably dressed in a tailored suit, exuded an air of cold detachment. His sharp features were unreadable, his presence commanding and intimidating. His piercing gaze settled on the silent woman opposite him, his eyes inscrutable.
“We’ll divorce on Monday,” he declared, his voice firm and emotionless. “Aside from the compensation in the agreement, you may request anything else you need.”
“Why so sudden?” Freya Briggs asked, her voice quieter than usual.
Kristian’s answer was blunt. “Ashley is back.”
Freya knew exactly who Ashley was. After a brief pause, she replied, “Okay.”
Kristian hesitated, caught off guard by her immediate acceptance.
Freya opened the divorce papers, her thoughts drifting to the past.
Two years ago, they had met at a nightclub. She had been weighed down by worries; he had been nursing a broken heart. A few drinks later, they found solace in each other’s company, talking late into the night.
There had been no impulsive one-night stand—just a quiet parting afterward.
Three days later, he had returned with his assistant to propose marriage. And she had agreed.
After getting married, he had treated her well—tending to her needs, drying her hair with gentle hands, and solving her problems before she even voiced them.
Their relationship had been perfect—until six months ago, when a single phone call changed everything.
Overnight, he grew distant, his warmth replaced by icy indifference. That was when she learned the truth: Kristian had married her because she bore a faint resemblance to his lost love, Ashley Bradley.
Check what’s new on g@lnovs.c○m
The memory made Freya press her lips together before she asked lightly, “You said I could ask for compensation, right?”
“Yes,” Kristian replied flatly.
“Anything I want?” She lifted her gaze to him, her delicate face devoid of its usual brightness.
For a fleeting moment, guilt flickered in his chest. “Yes.” He had already resolved to grant her reasonable demands.
After all, she had been good to him all this time.
Freya’s voice was steady. “Then I want the most expensive car in your garage.”
“Fine,” Kristian agreed.
“A villa in the suburbs,” she added.
“Done,” he said.
Freya smiled. “And a share of the money you’ve earned in the last two years.”
For the first time, Kristian’s composure cracked. His eyes narrowed slightly, as if questioning whether he’d heard correctly. “What did you say?”
Freya, unfazed, repeated her demand. “Our earnings during the marriage count as marital property, don’t they? Based on my calculations—excluding investments—your salary and dividends over the last two years amount to several billion. I don’t want much—just 40%.”
A heavy silence settled between them.
Then, she added, as if casually mentioning the weather, “Of course, you’re welcome to take 40% of my income too.”
Kristian’s patience finally snapped. “Freya!” His voice carried an edge of disbelief.
Had he really felt guilty earlier? How had he never noticed her greed?
Freya met his gaze evenly. “Is that not acceptable?”
“Absolutely not.”
Kristian dismissed the idea instantly.
“Then forget it.” Freya set down her pen. “Next time I see your family, I’ll bring up your emotional infidelity. I’m sure they’ll take my side.”
Kristian’s expression darkened, his stare turning glacial. He hadn’t anticipated this side of her—realizing now that her past docility had been an act.
“Do you really want to negotiate with me like this?” he demanded.
“Yes.” Freya held his gaze without flinching. She knew he despised threats—but she despised infidelity more.
“Fine.” Kristian’s eyes turned stormy, his voice glacial. “You’ll get what you want. But if the divorce hits complications, you’ll regret it.”
Freya leaned back in her chair, her tone razor-sharp. “Kristian Shaw, is that a threat?”
This version of her was foreign to Kristian. For two years, she had been the picture of compliance—gentle, accommodating, never defiant. Now, she met his anger with unshakable calm.
“No. Already calculating countermeasures,” he bit out. “You’ll have the assets. We divorce on Monday.”
Freya’s lashes lowered briefly before she added, “One more condition.”
“Speak.” His patience frayed.
“Take me shopping tomorrow.” She ignored the frost radiating from him. “Afterward, we’ll tell your family together that I ended things.”
“Deal,” Kristian conceded.
With that, he strode toward the door, unable to stomach another second in her presence.
Earlier, he’d even considered granting her a grace period to process the divorce.
How laughable. She couldn’t wait to carve up his fortune and be rid of him.
Had Freya been able to read his thoughts, she might have laughed and said, “That little money? Do you really think I care?”
Kristian reached the door and halted. Without turning around, he said, “I won’t be back tonight. I’ll pick you up at nine tomorrow morning. Make a list of the stores you want to visit.”
Freya’s voice followed him, calm but laced with something sharp. “Are you going to see Ashley Bradley?”
Kristian’s jaw tightened. “That’s none of your business.”
Freya let out a quiet breath, as if she had already expected that answer. “I don’t tolerate cheating,” she said plainly. “So before the divorce is finalized, you’d better not end up in bed with her.”
Kristian whirled back, looming over her.
Freya didn’t blink. “What? Can’t endure two more days?”
“I understand your bitterness,” he said, eerily composed, “but lashing out won’t help. This is a divorce, not war.”
Freya blinked at him. For a moment, she was at a loss for words. This man was truly shameless.
Kristian didn’t wait for a response. “Good night.” And with that, he turned and left.
The door clicked shut behind him.
Freya’s gaze drifted down to the divorce papers still lying on the table. She stood there for a long time, unmoving.
To say she felt nothing would have been a lie. She wasn’t made of stone.
The moment she discovered she was nothing more than a stand-in, the hurt settled deep in her bones.
Kristian had been her first love. In twenty-four years, no one else had breached her defenses. Before the betrayal, he had been perfection itself—attentive, steady, silencing every doubt with his quiet devotion. So when she learned of Ashley, she had offered to leave. To free him. But he had refused.

###Chapter 2
Chapter 2:
The reason behind Kristian’s refusal was simple. Before Ashley returned, he needed someone to manage his elders at home—and Freya, adored by his parents and grandpa, was the obvious choice. But sometimes, Freya couldn’t help but wonder—did he really think she was a fool? Otherwise, why would he assume she’d play along in hiding his affair?
Now, with his sudden demand for divorce, frustration simmered inside her.
Even after six months of steeling herself, a stubborn flicker of emotion remained.
She let out a slow breath, crossed to the sofa, and grabbed her phone. She tapped the contact labeled “Fred”—untouched for two years—and typed, “Check if Shaw Group’s facing any issues. And find out if Kristian’s terminally ill.”
Fred’s replies exploded onto the screen instantly.
“Holy—Freya?!”
“Never thought I’d hear from you again!”
“Two years, Freya. Two.”
“Where’ve you been?!”
She didn’t bother explaining.
Mood sour, she fired back a single word, “Check.”
Fred caved. “On it!”
She tossed the phone aside and waited.
If Kristian was divorcing her to spare her some tragedy, she’d forgive him—maybe even help. But if he was just an unfaithful jerk? She’d drop him without a second thought.
Thirty minutes later, her phone buzzed with Fred’s verdict. “Zero troubles. No illness, no crisis. Why the hell are you asking? Kristian’s loaded, hot, and sharp—you two are a match. Don’t you like pretty boys? Give it a shot!”

###Chapter 4

###Chapter 791
Chapter 791:
How could a boy ask a girl that? It had been painfully awkward.
He wanted to deny ever knowing Ellis if anyone brought that story up.
When the girl heard Ellis’s question, she’d said instinctively, “Shouldn’t boys protect girls?”
“I’m not like them. I only like people who can defeat me and protect me.”
That was Ellis’s infamous reply. Locke remembered every word of it. And the sheer deadpan delivery made it even worse. It was absolutely mortifying.
“Finish your tasks first—then we’ll talk,” Ellis said, giving nothing away.
Locke was speechless.
Just as he’d suspected, Ellis was as cryptic as ever.
“Is the woman stronger than you?” Locke tried a different tactic. “Does she have eight-pack abs, biceps like rocks, and bench presses cars? Could she toss you over her shoulder?”
Ellis didn’t even bother replying. What kind of nonsense was that?
“You’re serious, aren’t you?” Locke took the silence as confirmation, his imagination running wild. “Mr. Lambert, your taste is… quite something.”
The mental image was too much. What if Ellis and that woman stood side by side? He would look like a fragile husband next to a battle-hardened heroine.
Locke couldn’t even begin to guess how Ellis’s parents would react to that.
“Focus on the task,” Ellis cut in sharply. “Don’t overthink. Fail this, and the test’s over.”
“Consider it done!” Locke’s confidence soared.
After ending the call, he immediately passed the news on to Ellis’s parents, Caldwell and Kendra.
It took the couple half an hour to absorb the information.

Kristian saw through Damian’s worries, knowing only time could mend his lack of confidence.

###Chapter 1787
Chapter 1787:
Meanwhile, in the quiet of the study downstairs, Ellis and Jesse sat opposite each other beneath the warm glow of a desk lamp.
Ellis looked up and asked plainly, “You know something, don’t you?”
Jesse met his gaze. “About Damian?”
Jesse shot her a look. “Seriously? That’s her thank-you for bailing her out?”
Nina glanced away. “Bailing her out? Please. He’s only making things worse.”
Jesse wasn’t finished. “I remember Mom and Dad saying they never wanted you marrying far from home. Jeucwell and Alerith are over a thousand miles apart. That’s not just far—it’s gone.”
Nina sulked, lips pressing into a pout.
“Damian’s cold,” Jesse continued, directing his words toward their parents. “Not the kind of man who knows how to take care of someone long-term. When he shows up tomorrow, you should shut the door on him.”
“Jesse!” Nina exploded, furious.
But Jesse stayed cool, unfazed by her temper.
Freya and Ellis, meanwhile, remained silent, letting their children’s bickering play itself out.
After dinner, Nina quietly sought out Freya, hopeful for a breakthrough. Her mother had always doted on her—surely that hadn’t changed.
She leaned in, eyes wide with earnest appeal, lashes fluttering like wings. “Mom, please don’t make things hard for Damian tomorrow,” she murmured. “He’s really wonderful.”
Freya’s voice was soft and reassuring. “We won’t. We just want to understand him a little better.”
Nina hesitated, then asked carefully, “You don’t care about family background… do you?”
“We don’t,” Freya responded without pause.
“Then… what exactly do you want to know about Damian?” Nina pressed, hoping to gather hints—anything to help Damian prepare. “I’ll see if he meets your standards.”
But Freya sidestepped with a knowing smile. “You’ll find out tomorrow. Your dad and I won’t be harsh. As long as he treats you well, we won’t .”
“He does! He really does treat me well,” Nina said a little too quickly, rushing to defend him.
Freya’s tone remained calm, almost teasing. “You adore him, so of course you think he’s amazing. But to know if he truly is, we need to see it for ourselves.”
“Mommy…” Nina whined playfully, trying to charm her way through.
Freya reached out and gently patted her head. “Be patient. Trust us.”
“Alright,” Nina relented with a small nod, but her heart still churned with unease.
Meanwhile, in the quiet of the study downstairs, Ellis and Jesse sat opposite each other beneath the warm glow of a desk lamp.
Ellis looked up and asked plainly, “You know something, don’t you?”
Jesse met his gaze. “About Damian?”
“If you and Mom put your foot down and strictly forbid Nina from seeing Damian, she won’t defy you,” Jesse said, his voice low with a plea he rarely made. “But it will crush her. She might never recover from it.”
“Don’t try to get words from me,” Ellis replied, his eyes narrowing with quiet insight. “Whether they can be together depends on what I see when I meet him.”
.
.

###Chapter 1788
Chapter 1788:
Jesse bit back a response. His father was not a man easily swayed.
Once outside the study, he found Nina waiting. They exchanged what little they had learned—confirming that prying information from their parents was like trying to draw water from stone.
“You told Dad about Damian…” Nina murmured, betraying the worry in her eyes. “Do you think he’ll forbid me from being with him because of it?”
“I’m not sure,” Jesse admitted with a shrug. He found it tough to guess what their parents were thinking. “But you know they adore you, so they’ll likely want to keep you happy.”
Nina’s face showed a flicker of concern. She used to feel certain her parents would support her relationship with Damian. Now, with the moment of truth approaching, nerves crept in.
“Mom’s easier to convince,” Nina said, her voice tinged with mixed feelings. “Dad, though, might be a tougher nut to crack.”
Ellis was usually laid-back, more like a friend than a strict parent. But on certain matters, he could turn firm, and few could sway him.
“Instead of fretting, maybe you should just call it quits with Damian now,” Jesse teased with a smirk.
Nina was momentarily stunned. “Watch your words,” she shot back, narrowing her eyes.
Jesse glanced at her but stayed quiet.
The next morning arrived, and Damian showed up with Kristian in tow.
Ellis and Freya were a bit surprised to see Kristian.
Freya welcomed them warmly, and they exchanged polite hellos, keeping things friendly yet slightly formal.
At first, the group chatted about light topics—politics, business, and how time slips away.
Nina, sitting close to Damian, grew restless with the small talk. “Let’s get to the point,” she suggested. “We can talk it over before lunch.”
“Alright,” Ellis said, looking relaxed but exuding confidence.
Damian had never met anyone with such a commanding presence.
“Are you Damian Bryant?” Ellis asked.
“Yes, Mr. Lambert,” Damian replied.
“You want to marry Nina, correct?” Ellis eased into the conversation.
Damian kept his cool. “Yes.”
“I’m fine with you dating Nina,” Ellis began warmly before getting serious. “But marriage is a big step, and as her parents, we need to think it through carefully.”
“I understand,” Damian said politely. “Feel free to ask me anything.”
“How do you view the gap in your and Nina’s family backgrounds?” Ellis asked, his eyes locked on Damian.
“Dad!” Nina blurted out.
Ellis glanced at her, his silence carrying weight.
Nina quickly fell quiet.
“There’s a clear difference,” Damian admitted openly. “A while back, I might’ve felt unworthy of her, but now I’m confident I can make her happy.”
.
.

###Chapter 1789
Chapter 1789:
Before arriving, doubts had clouded his mind. But standing here, clarity washed over him.
Nina had always been the bold one in their relationship. As her partner, he needed to step up and be even braver.
“What if we don’t approve because of this gap?” Ellis pressed.
Nina opened her mouth to speak, but Jesse subtly nudged her arm. His eyes signaled for her to hold back.
Nina’s worry grew. Damian was sensitive about this issue, and her father’s words might make him pull away.
Jesse, however, believed that if Damian couldn’t handle this, he wasn’t right for Nina. He saw why his dad was pushing this point. If Damian couldn’t face these challenges, their marriage might crumble later. Marriage was a different beast from dating. A divorce would hit Nina hard, and finding someone to mend her heart wouldn’t be easy.
“I’d respect your choice,” Damian said honestly, a spark of realization in his voice. “But I’ll work hard to prove I’m worthy so that you can see past our different backgrounds.” He spoke with conviction.
Nina’s eyes widened in surprise.
“We only have one daughter, and we can’t bear the thought of her moving far away,” Ellis said, sizing Damian up. “Would you consider living with us?”
Nina blinked, caught off guard.
Damian glanced at Nina, then answered thoughtfully, “I could do that.”
“Really?” Ellis asked, his tone steady.
“Yes,” Damian nodded. “But I’d likely only stay here on weekends and holidays. My work in Jeucwell keeps me there during the week.”
“You could leave your job and work with us here,” Ellis suggested.
He added, “You could manage Briggs Group, Lambert Group, and Anita International.”
Damian paused, surprised. “Anita International? Does that belong to Nina’s family?”
“Yes,” Ellis replied, his voice calm and warm.
“I’m grateful for Uncle Kristian’s mentorship, so I’ll only work at Shaw Group,” Damian said firmly, still fighting for his future with Nina. “But I promise to travel here every Friday after work to be with Nina and leave early Monday.” The schedule would be grueling, but he was willing to make it work.
Nina sighed softly. “Mom…”
The thought of weekly flights exhausted her. She hated the idea of Damian wearing himself out.
Freya wanted to chime in but held back, unsure if it was her place.
Noticing the servant bringing fruit, she got an idea. She stood, grabbed the tray, and discreetly texted Nina: “Your dad’s just testing him. He won’t make it too hard.”
The first question was to ensure Damian wouldn’t abandon Nina over family differences.
The second checked his loyalty and gratitude. Everyone in their circle knew Kristian had shaped Damian’s career. Neither giving up Nina for his job nor abandoning his career for her would’ve been ideal. Damian’s response struck the perfect balance.
Reading the text, Nina let out a relieved breath and smiled as she took the fruit from Freya.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1790
Chapter 1790:
Ellis caught their exchange, a faint smile tugging at his lips, but he didn’t let on. “This setup might strain your relationship,” Ellis warned, testing Damian’s resolve. “I’d prefer you resign and work here in Alerith.”
“No need for that,” Kristian cut in, reading Ellis’s intentions. “Shaw Group has a branch in Alerith. We can move the headquarters here.”
“But…” Damian hesitated.
Kristian, with his usual charm, insisted, “Trust me on this.” He shot Damian a knowing look.
Damian caught on instantly, realizing this was all part of the test.
Even so, Damian took Ellis’s words seriously.
He spoke with genuine sincerity as he looked at Ellis. “Uncle Kristian was just teasing. Jeucwell is the Shaw Group’s base—there’s no way the headquarters could be moved. But I’ll do everything I can to balance my work and my relationship with Nina. You can count on that.”
“Let’s go upstairs and talk,” Ellis said, already quite satisfied.
There was no denying Damian’s sincerity.
Even with Kristian dropping hints, Damian had chosen to respond with complete honesty. Now he understood what his daughter saw in this man.
“Dad,” Nina said, a little cautiously, “can I come with you two?”
“No need.”
“If you get thirsty while talking, I can pour some coffee for you,” offered Nina. “I’ve got hands.”
Nina pouted, her lips pushing out in visible annoyance. She didn’t want to leave Damian alone, afraid he might get grilled upstairs. She tried again, reluctantly. “Then let Mom join in. Damian’s here to talk to both of you, not just you.”
“They can talk on their own,” Freya said gently, clearly unwilling to go. They’d already decided the night before that Ellis would be the one to speak with Damian, and she had no intention of interfering.
“Mom,” Nina pleaded softly.
“Don’t worry,” Freya said, patting her on the head.
In the end, Nina gave in.
Ellis led Damian upstairs to the study. Inside that quiet, private space, Damian looked visibly more tense than before.
Ellis poured him a cup of coffee, calm and casual. “Have a seat.”
“Thank you,” Damian said with a slight nod.
They sat across from each other on single-seaters by the floor-to-ceiling window.
“Don’t be nervous,” Ellis said plainly. “We don’t have any ion to you being with Nina, but there’s something I need to ask.”
“Please, go ahead.” Damian felt a touch of relief.
Ellis gave him a steady look, his voice still casual. “I heard you’ve been treated for excessive control and possessiveness?”
“Yes,” Damian didn’t try to hide it.
“Would you mind telling me a bit about it?” Ellis asked, giving him space. He wouldn’t push—he understood how personal psychological struggles could be. But as Nina’s father, he needed clarity.
Damian’s fingers tensed slightly, though his expression stayed calm. “No, I don’t mind.”
.
.

###Chapter 1791
Chapter 1791:
“What was the worst it ever got?” Ellis had a sharp eye for emotion. He could see the strain Damian was hiding. “Just a simple explanation will do. Don’t tense up.”
Damian pressed his lips together, remembering those dark thoughts. He opened his mouth, hesitated, then paused again. Would Nina’s father still accept him after hearing this?
“If it’s too difficult, you don’t have to say,” Ellis said gently, seeing the turmoil in him.
“I wanted her all to myself,” Damian finally admitted, lowering his gaze. His voice was husky. “I wanted to lock her away. I wanted her world to revolve around me and no one else.”
These were things he hadn’t even told Nina. At one point, he’d even looked up ways online to keep her close without drawing suspicion. He’d hated himself for it.
Ellis’s face stayed neutral. When he’d first heard about Damian’s need for treatment, he’d figured the problem had gone deeper than ordinary jealousy. “So why didn’t you act on it?” That was the question that mattered most to Ellis.
“I don’t know,” Damian replied honestly. “Maybe I didn’t want to see her scared or crying. Or maybe… she was just too good to be treated that way.”
He didn’t have a neat answer. He only knew that every time those impulses surfaced, guilt hit him just as hard. That conflict, over time, had made his emotions unstable—so he’d sought help.
“And now?” Ellis asked calmly.
“Now… those feelings are still there, a little. But I can control them.” Damian took a breath. “And more than anything, I want her to be happy.”
Ellis looked at him for a moment. “What does she mean to you?”
“She’s my anchor. My peace,” Damian answered without missing a beat. In his heart, he added silently—she was his light, brightening up every dark corner of his world.
“We don’t have any ions to your relationship with her,” Ellis said sincerely.
“Just one thing.”
“Please tell me.” Damian was still bracing himself.
“Cherish her—truly,” Ellis said firmly. “She’s been spoiled by us, and she can be a bit willful at times. I hope you’ll be patient with her.”
“She’s amazing,” Damian replied at once.
Ellis smiled, then stood and gave Damian’s shoulder a firm pat. “You’re great too. Be confident.”
That one simple sentence struck something deep in Damian—giving him a sense of strength he didn’t know he needed.
“Let’s head down,” Ellis said. From the moment Damian had arrived, he’d sensed the man’s lack of confidence. “If we stay any longer, Nina will think I’m giving you a hard time.”
“Mr. Lambert,” Damian called after him suddenly.
Ellis paused. “Yes?”
“I’ll take good care of Nina. I won’t let her get hurt,” Damian promised, his voice steady. “You have my word.”
“I believe you,” Ellis said. From what he’d seen of Damian before, and everything he’d heard now, he had a solid impression of him. “But if your emotions ever start spiraling again, be honest with her. Get help. Talk it through.”
.
.

###Chapter 1792
Chapter 1792:
“Okay,” Damian said with a nod.
They stepped out of the study.
As soon as Nina saw them coming down, she rushed over. Her eyes bounced between the two, anxious. “What did you talk about? Why were you gone so long?”
Damian’s face didn’t give anything away. She was growing restless.
“I offered him money to leave you,” Ellis joked as he reached the last step. “We haggled for a while.”
Nina rolled her eyes. “You’re so childish.”
“You don’t believe me?” Ellis raised a brow.
“If you pay him to leave me, I’ll pay Mom to leave you,” Nina shot back. “Let’s be honest—when it comes to making her happy, I’m way better than you.”
Ellis lifted his eyes with a smile in his voice. “You really think you’re better at making her happy than I am?”
Nina wanted to agree, yet the words stalled on her tongue, weighed down by the thought of how her answer might affect their feelings.
Instead, she turned to her mother with a playful glint. “Mom, am I better at making you happy than Dad?”
Freya didn’t hesitate. She smiled softly and nodded. “You do.”
Nina’s face lit up like sunlight breaking through clouds. “Did you hear that?” she asked, brimming with pride.
Ellis, lounging in quiet amusement, replied with a dry chuckle. “She’s just letting you win.”
Nina’s smile faltered. She had no comeback. She couldn’t deny he was right. No one else could move mountains just to see her mother smile other than her father.
In most couples, affection dulled with the years, settling into the monotony of middle age, but her parents’ love still burned steady and sweet—enough to make anyone envy it.
“What did you say to Damian, exactly?” she asked, steering the conversation away, sidling up beside Damian with casual grace. “Did my dad give you a hard time?”
“Not at all,” Damian replied, genuinely. “He’s quite nice to me.”
Nina’s eyes slid to Ellis. Coming from Damian, that was high praise. Still, she couldn’t help but wonder—had they really not talked about anything upstairs?
Ellis’s deep voice rolled out at an unhurried pace. “Didn’t you want to take Kristian to that restaurant? It’s mealtime now—let’s go.”
“Oh, yes!” Her mood shifted instantly, her eyes brightening. “Let’s go eat.” The restaurant sat only a short drive from her home, famed for its refined dishes.
Nina dined there several times a month.
Twenty minutes later, they were settling into a secluded yard of a hilltop villa.
The restaurant itself was an architectural gem, serving just seven tables a day. Exclusive, peaceful, and tucked away from the noise of the world.
“Dad, come with me to pick out the ingredients,” Nina said, rising from her seat and beckoning Ellis. “See which ones you like.”
He rose without comment.
Then, Nina turned to Jesse and Damian. “You two head to the wine cellar and grab something from Room One—they’re ours.”
With the instructions handed off, she and Ellis disappeared down the stone path.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1793
Chapter 1793:
Ellis settled on a long stone bench in the corridor that framed the old architectural hallways, his long coat draped effortlessly around him, the soft winter light catching the sharp lines of his silhouette. “I’ll wait for you here.”
“You’re not going?” Nina asked.
“Nope.”
“You should. Didn’t you personally pick the ingredients last time?”
Ellis shot her a look. “Don’t think I don’t see what you’re doing.” He’d read her like an open book. Casually, almost lazily, he laid her scheme bare. “You just want to get us out of the way.”
Nina gave an awkward cough. He’d caught her clean.
Ellis shook his head, mildly amused. “You really want to leave your mom alone with Kristian?”
That wasn’t something he expected from her.
“They haven’t seen each other in years,” Nina said, sliding onto the seat beside him, her tone softening as if to ease his mood. “There’s probably a lot they need to say. You see my mom every day—what’s a little alone time between old friends?”
Ellis raised an eyebrow. “So, what now? You trying to become Kristian’s daughter?”
“I wouldn’t mind,” Nina quipped, unable to resist teasing.
“The base is short on new recruits,” Ellis said, playing along. “You might just qualify.”
“I still think I’d rather be your daughter,” she replied with a grin.
Ellis smirked. “Then when are you joining? I’ll tailor a training program just for you.”
Nina leaned back dramatically. “Dad…”
He gave her head a gentle tap. “Your mom’s never been the best conversationalist. Leaving her alone with Kristian? That’s just cruel.”
Nina scratched the back of her head, sheepish. “You’re right.”
She’d been so focused on what Kristian might be feeling, she hadn’t thought about how her mom might handle the silence.
Ellis watched her expression shift, then flicked her lightly on the forehead. “And you call yourself the expert at making her happy?”
“I just didn’t think it all the way through,” she admitted.
Nina muttered defensively, “You distracted me—taking Damian upstairs like that!”
“Oh, so now it’s my fault?” Ellis arched a brow, his tone rising slightly.
Nina was quick on her feet. “Totally my fault.”
Ellis didn’t push the point. “Go pick the ingredients yourself. I’m heading back.”
She nodded and watched him walk away. His tall, straight figure moved with an ease that was both confident and magnetic, and for a moment, a tangle of emotions welled in her chest. Her parents felt like the better match. Kristian and her mom were both reserved. If they spent the rest of their lives together, they might run out of words.
Ellis, though… he might seem aloof, but around her mother, he came alive. Always with something to say.
And thankfully, she herself was a chatterbox in disguise too. With Damian around, boredom wouldn’t be an issue in her future.
.
.

###Chapter 1794
Chapter 1794:
Inside the quiet yard, the air carried the faint scent of wine from the kitchen. After Jesse and Damian left to fetch the bottles, only Freya and Kristian remained.
So many years had passed that the old shadows no longer clung to their hearts. They could now sit together and speak with the ease of old friends.
“Damian is a good man,” Kristian remarked, his warm, familiar voice coloring his tone. “I’ve watched him grow up. You can feel at ease letting Nina be with him.”
Freya gave a small nod.
Since childhood, Nina had spoken often of Damian, and as she grew older, his name still found its way into her conversations. She understood her daughter’s feelings for him all too well.
“Are you truly thinking of letting Damian take over the Shaw Group?” she asked, steering the conversation elsewhere.
“He’s more than capable,” Kristian replied without hesitation. “With him there, I’ll have nothing to worry about.”
Freya nodded again, and for a moment, silence settled between them.
Kristian’s gaze lingered on her, unguarded, before he finally voiced what had been sitting in his heart for years. “Seeing how strong your bond with Ellis still is… I’m relieved.”
“And you?” Freya asked softly.
“What about me?”
“Why haven’t you remarried?”
He paused, then answered plainly, without deflection. “I don’t see the need. I’ve yet to figure out the meaning of life for myself—why involve someone else in that?”
Then he added with a dry, almost playful edge, “Besides, I couldn’t let another woman take the place of the one you once were.”
He had let her go after she married, but letting go didn’t mean he ever stopped loving her.
Over the years, his parents had introduced him to many women—graceful, charming, and kind. Some he genuinely liked. But none stirred him deeply enough to marry.
His heart still belonged to Freya. Without her, he simply couldn’t imagine a life shared with anyone else. Nor did he want to repeat the folly of his youth: neglecting someone he loved while chasing the shadow of someone he’d already lost. So, he remained single.
“She wouldn’t become the woman I once was,” Freya stated firmly.
Her love for Ellis was real. And even if it wasn’t—even if Ellis abandoned her—she would never return to Kristian, nor try to rekindle what they once had. She would continue walking the path she had chosen, and no matter how steep or thorny, she would not turn back. She had no regrets.
Kristian looked at Freya, and a flicker of emotion stirred somewhere deep inside him. He still admired that fierce, unyielding spirit of hers.
“Freya,” he called her name suddenly.
Freya lifted her gaze and asked, “What is it?”
“If, back then, I hadn’t treated you like that… if I’d made the choice without hesitation and picked you instead of Ashley—would you still have walked away from me?” His voice was casual, effortless, as though he were just making conversation.
Freya shot right back, “Well, by that logic—if Ashley had really left you because of a terminal illness, would you have chosen her… or me?”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1795
Chapter 1795:
Kristian didn’t answer right away. His eyes lowered, and after a moment of silence, he said, “I don’t know.”
If it were him now, the answer would be easy—he’d choose Freya in a heartbeat. But back then, he hadn’t grown into the man he was now. At that time, he’d been tangled in guilt toward Ashley, desperate to make amends. But unless he was forced to confront that situation directly, he hadn’t known what “making amends” truly meant.
“That’s why we were never right for each other,” Freya said softly, her words a quiet conclusion.
“If Ellis had an unforgettable ex-girlfriend, what choice would he make if he were faced with something like that?” Kristian asked seriously.
Just then, Ellis made his way over. Without missing a beat, he took a seat beside Freya, laced his fingers through hers, and said, “I’d choose her. No hesitation.”
After that, not much else was said.
The air remained still and silent—until Nina and the others came back and life seemed to hum again.
It was half past twelve. They all sat down to lunch together.
After the topic of Damian and Nina’s marriage was discussed, Kristian and Damian didn’t stay too long. They lingered for a short while in the afternoon, had a light chat, and then headed out.
Not long after they’d gone, Nina picked up on the odd shift in the atmosphere from earlier.
She asked Freya and Ellis tentatively, “What did you talk about with Uncle Kristian while we were out?”
“Nothing,” Ellis replied, clearly unwilling to say more.
To Nina, Kristian was family. He cared about her deeply.
She said bluntly, “Nothing? Yeah, I’m not buying that. Something definitely felt off.”
“If you’ve got the time to dwell on that, why not focus on what you’ll say to Jerome when you see him later?” Ellis said, smoothly redirecting.
Nina blinked, caught off guard. “Jerome’s coming?”
“He messaged you,” Ellis said. “Didn’t you check your phone?”
Nina froze, suddenly remembering that she’d left her phone with Damian during lunch.
Now he understood why Damian had been giving her those strange looks. He’d already seen the message and knew Jerome was coming tonight. Without wasting another second, she grabbed her phone to call Jerome and ask when he’d be arriving, then snatched her car keys and dashed out. Meanwhile, Damian returned to the hotel.
Soon after, he received an invitation from Jerome.
Given everything between him and Nina, Damian didn’t hesitate. He accepted right away.
They met at a club. Along with them, Nick and Kyra were also there.
One look was all it took—Damian instantly understood why Jerome had asked him here.
“Nina’s a treasure to all of us,” Jerome said, seated across from Damian, his sharp eyes glinting. “Since she chose you, we want to see if you’re really worthy of her.”
Damian didn’t reply. He simply gestured for them to continue. At that moment, he realized one thing: Even if he was usually filled with self-doubt, now, he had all the courage he needed to fight for her.
.
.

###Chapter 1796
Chapter 1796:
“You’re the CEO of the Shaw Group. Socializing’s part of the job,” Jerome said, glancing at the drinks on the table. “If you can outdrink us, I’ll give you my blessing to be with Nina.”
To Jerome, this was a test of reliability. There were plenty of people in the business world who lost control once they’d had a few drinks—he just didn’t know if Damian was one of them, so he had to find out.
“Alright,” Damian agreed without pause.
Kyra elbowed Nick.
Nick looked puzzled, not quite following her cue.
Kyra shot him a glare. They both knew Damian was a lightweight. The last time in Jeucwell, Damian had passed out before Nick even got properly buzzed.
Nick glanced from Jerome to Damian, then leaned over and muttered to Kyra, “Let them drink. There’s always tension between them anyway—typical of love rivals.”
“Did you forget Jerome said we’re all drinking with Damian?”
Kyra hissed, gritting her teeth. “It’s not just the two of them.”
“If I win, I have one condition,” Damian suddenly said.
Jerome leaned in slightly, his voice even. “Say it.”
“Come back once a year for Nina’s birthday,” Damian said, eyes locked on Jerome’s. “She cares about you a lot.”
Everyone went quiet.
Nick looked baffled.
Kyra looked equally thrown.
They were all confused. None of them had seen that coming.
“Alright,” Jerome agreed.
“Are you dumb or what?”
Nick blurted, giving Damian a look of disbelief. “Even if you hadn’t said it, Jerome would’ve done that anyway.”
Ever since they’d met, Nick had never once seen Jerome miss Nina’s birthday. Actually, not just her birthday. He never missed any important occasion in her life.
Jerome glanced over at Nick. Was his friend taking his rival’s side?
Nick obviously supported Jerome. He scratched his head, suddenly feeling awkward.
“If you win, I’ll feel okay stepping back. I’ll stop loving her,” Jerome added quietly.
“No need to stop,” Damian replied calmly, a master at psychological warfare. “Keep loving her. The more people who care about her, the more warmth she feels.”
“Are you insane?”
Nick finally snapped.
Damian didn’t say a word.
Only Jerome truly understood what he meant.
Damian was telling him to keep loving Nina, but watch her build a life with someone else. A quiet kind of torment. One that would last a lifetime. Could this man really give Nina peace and happiness?
“How are we doing this?” Damian asked, his tone cool and composed. “All of us drink together, or one-on-one?”
“I’ll go first,” Jerome said.
.
.

###Chapter 1797
Chapter 1797:
“Alright,” Damian replied.
They came to an agreement.
After that, the two of them began drinking.
Round after round. And as the drinks flowed, everyone around them held their breath.
“Jerome can hold his liquor way better than Damian,” murmured Kyra as she sat beside Nick, her voice tinged with unease. “Is it really okay to let them keep drinking like this?”
“It’s just a little competition; don’t stress,” Nick replied confidently, brushing off her concern.
Jerome and Damian weren’t regular drinkers, and both were in good physical shape. Occasional drinking wouldn’t do any harm.
“You stay here and keep an eye on them. I’m heading out to call Nina,” Kyra said, clearly worried. Both men were important to Nina, and this wasn’t sitting well with her. “Try to find a way to slow down their drinking.”
“No need…” Nick muttered, thinking this was something the two men could handle themselves.
“Do as I say,” Kyra insisted, not giving him a choice.
Nick scratched the back of his head. “Alright…”
Moments later, noticing the two still knocking back drinks one after another, Nick finally took action as Kyra had asked.
“Why not take a break?” he chimed in as they set their glasses down. “Drinking like this is brutal on the body. How about throwing in a game or something to slow things down?”
“I’m good with it. He can decide,” Jerome said, calm and composed.
Damian’s gaze sharpened slightly as he placed his glass on the table. “What kind of game?”
“Each of you share something meaningful about your time with Nina,” Nick suggested, clearly making it up on the fly. He had no idea how to run a game like this. “We’ll be the judges. The loser takes a drink.”
“Alright,” Jerome said.
“Alright,” Damian echoed.

Jerome smiled and continued to enjoy the meal by her side.
If he were truly blessed, he wouldn’t lose the girl he loved deeply.
Jerome glanced upward as the thought crossed his mind, his eyes landing on Nina, who was quietly focused on her meal. Just before her gaze lifted to meet his, he quickly looked away.
They kept eating, exchanging casual words now and then.
Half an hour later, they settled the bill and stepped outside.
With over three hours left before boarding, Nina stayed by his side for a while. At first, their conversation stayed light, but then Jerome turned to her and asked, “What kind of woman do you think my future wife will be like?”
“Whoever you fancy,” Nina answered plainly, without skipping a beat. “That’s who she’ll be.”
Jerome gave a low chuckle but didn’t say anything more.
After meeting someone like Nina—so striking, so full of life—it had become harder for him to imagine anyone else stirring his heart the same way. After all, not everyone walked through life carrying the kind of sunshine she did, lighting up every room with her effortless, cheerful smile.
“Jerome,” she called softly.
“What?”
“One day, we’re all going to find our own happiness,” Nina said, her voice steady. “You, Jesse, Jasper—we all will.”
Everyone, in time, would meet the right person. Someone to love, someone to grow old with.
“Yes.” Jerome nodded, glancing at his watch. It was about time to board. He didn’t linger. “I should check in. Take good care of yourself while you’re here.”
“Okay,” Nina replied.
Jerome’s eyes lingered on her face, dark and unreadable beneath the weight of emotion.
Nina met his gaze.
But before she could say a word, she suddenly found herself wrapped in a warm, tight embrace.
Jerome held her close, resting his chin on her shoulder, his voice low and husky as he murmured, “Call me if you ever need anything. I’ll be around. Always.”
“You too,” Nina said, returning the hug. “Take care of yourself.” His grip tightened ever so slightly.
After a quiet moment, he pulled himself together and said, “I’m going.” With that, he let go, picked up his suitcase, and walked away.
Nina stood there, watching his figure retreat into the crowd, silently wishing him well.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1809
Chapter 1809:
She didn’t quite understand the ache of being let go by someone who didn’t choose you. Nor could she fully grasp Jerome’s sadness or the tangled emotions he carried as he left. But she knew one thing—he must’ve been hurting deeply.
After all, that hug had said it all.
She didn’t leave right away. Instead, she waited until his flight had taken off.
Quietly, in her heart, she offered a silent blessing. “Jerome, may everything go your way.”
Once the plane disappeared into the sky, Nina finally turned and left the airport. On her way to meet Damian, she sent a brief message to Jesse. “Jerome has left.”
Jesse didn’t respond immediately—he was tangled up in a thorny issue. He hadn’t dealt with one like this before.
Not waiting for his reply, Nina turned her attention to her group chat with her friends.
The conversation was short, and soon she arrived at the hotel.
Almost immediately, the hotel manager approached with a courteous smile and asked, “Miss Lambert, are you here to see Kristian Shaw and Damian Bryant?”
“Yes,” Nina answered with a nod.
“They’ve already left,” the manager informed her.
Nina blinked in surprise. “Left?”
“Yes,” the manager confirmed. “They checked out about two hours ago. Mr. Shaw asked me to let you know they would leave the city today and that you shouldn’t worry.”
“Thank you,” Nina said quickly, though unease had begun to settle in her chest. She couldn’t help but worry. She had just sent Jerome off, and now Damian had left. It was hard not to assume Damian had misunderstood. Maybe he thought she cared more about Jerome. Maybe he’d gotten upset and left in frustration.
As soon as she got in the car, she told the driver to head to the airport. While on the way, she called Damian. Luckily, the airport wasn’t as far as the one Jerome flew out from—otherwise, she might not have made it in time.
When the call went through, a beep sounded from the other end.
Hearing it, she let out a quiet breath of relief.
Thank goodness—he hadn’t boarded yet.
The phone rang once before Damian picked up. Before he could even say a word, Nina spoke in a rush. “I’m on my way to the airport. Wait for me there—I’ll go with you.”
“No need,” Damian replied, his tone calm.
“I’m really coming,” Nina insisted, glancing at the time, her voice filled with urgency.
Damian’s voice was warm and steady. “We’re boarding in ten minutes. Go home and get some rest. I’ll come see you when I’m free.”
“I won’t leave you alone at the hotel again, I swear,” Nina promised quickly, trying to ease whatever emotions he might be feeling. “Please, just wait for me.”
“I’m not upset.”
“Then why did you leave without saying goodbye?”
“I was afraid,” Damian admitted quietly, “that if I said goodbye, I wouldn’t be able to go.”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1810
Chapter 1810:
He’d been changing—slowly, silently—for Nina.
She was a free spirit, and while she might’ve been willing to give her freedom up for him, he didn’t want her to.
She deserved to be happy.
Freer, even, than before. Being with him shouldn’t take that away.
Nina furrowed her brows, unsure. “What do you mean?”
“Your home is in Alerith,” Damian explained. “That’s where your home is. You have family and friends there. We’ll do the long-distance thing for now. I’ll visit when I can.”
“I want to go with you—”
Before she could finish, Damian cut in softly, “Be good.”
Nina paused. The words caught her off guard.
Staying in Jeucwell for Damian had always been her choice. She didn’t feel burdened. She wasn’t unhappy. But something about his voice—firm yet tender—warmed her. Was this what love really felt like?
“I’m boarding now,” Damian said gently. “Stay in Alerith for a while. I’ll come to you when I’ve wrapped things up.”
Nina didn’t respond. She couldn’t tell if he truly meant it or if he was forcing himself to let go.
As if sensing her hesitation, Damian added one last thing before ending the call. “I’m serious. If you don’t believe me, ask Kristian.”
“Are you really not waiting for me?” Nina asked quietly.
“Next time,” Damian replied.
And just like that, they both went silent—each holding onto their own thoughts—before ending the call.
Still uncertain, Nina messaged Kristian. She knew he wouldn’t lie to her. “Is Damian okay emotionally? Is something wrong?”
Kristian’s reply was brief. “He’s fine. Don’t worry.”
Nina frowned. “Really?”
After a moment, Kristian responded again. “He’s learning to love you.”
Those words lit up Nina’s screen—and something deep within her chest.
At that moment, Damian sent Nina a message—something that didn’t quite fit his usual style. “You’ve done so much for me, and I want to give something back. Keep being yourself when you are with me.”
Thinking back over this period, he knew Nina had given up a great deal for him. She used to love hanging out with friends, but she’d cut ties with them because of him, leaving only him in her world. She had always enjoyed the liveliness of a crowd, yet now she stayed with him all day long and never once got bored. He used to worry that her love for him would fade once the novelty wore off. But now, that fear had vanished. He knew deep down—she really did love him. Her family, her friends—each of them wonderful people. Even Jerome…
Nina sent back a message, heartfelt and direct. “I don’t want a long-distance relationship.”
Just as Damian boarded the plane, he replied, “I’ll come find you. Until then, enjoy yourself like before. Once I get there, then spend all your time with me.”
Seeing his reply, Nina texted back, “Okay.”
.
.
.

###Chapter 1811
Chapter 1811:
She put away her phone, told the driver to head home, and looked out the window quietly.
To most people, Damian seemed moody and manipulative, constantly draining Nina’s care and patience. But the truth was, he was just overly sensitive and insecure. Rather than risk getting hurt, he chose to push things away before they could hurt him first. When he gave himself fully to love, though, he became someone truly wonderful.
He wouldn’t make the same mistake twice. And he always considered her feelings. More than anything, she was the only person in his heart.
By six o’clock, Nina got home.
Ellis and Freya were a little surprised to see her return, and Freya asked straight away, “Weren’t you supposed to go to Jeucwell with Damian?” They had received a message from Damian earlier, saying that he was leaving Alerith. So how come Nina was back now?
“He went back with Uncle Kristian and told me to stay here and spend time with you two,” Nina replied, not mentioning that they hadn’t even said goodbye. She didn’t want her parents worrying about her relationship.
Ellis said casually, “We’re planning a trip, so there’s no need to stick around just for us. If you want to go to Jeucwell, go. If you want to work, pick any position at the company.”
“I’ve never seen a father who’s so eager to get rid of his daughter,” Nina retorted.
Ellis lifted his gaze slightly, his voice casual as always. “First time seeing someone so keen on being a third wheel.”
The words Nina had been about to say got caught in her throat. Sometimes she really wondered how her parents managed to stay so in love after all these years. When she and Damian reached their age, maybe their fiery passion would cool, leaving behind something steady and lasting.
“I don’t want to be a third wheel,” Nina said honestly, not intending to intrude.
“What is it?” Freya asked, instantly concerned.
Nina looked at Ellis, then walked over to Freya, hooked her arm, and leaned on her affectionately. “Can we talk upstairs?”
“Sure,” Freya agreed without hesitation.
The two of them headed upstairs. Watching them go with soft eyes, Ellis began checking over the travel itinerary.
In the upstairs bedroom, Freya noticed Nina hesitating and said, “Just say what’s on your mind.”
“I heard that you and Dad both proposed to each other?” Nina said, having heard the story from Greta and Alan. “Is that actually true?”
Freya nodded. “Yes.”
“I want to propose to Damian,” Nina said, her bright eyes filled with anticipation. “Do you have any tips or suggestions?”
Freya paused for a moment and echoed the word softly. “Propose?”
“Yes,” Nina nodded.
Freya looked a little conflicted.
Nina blinked, still looking utterly adorable. “What’s wrong?”
“It’s better if Damian proposes,” Freya said after a moment of thought. “You don’t need to rush it.”
No wonder Damian had messaged them earlier, asking them to stop Nina if she planned on proposing to him.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1812
Chapter 1812:
Nina was caught off guard, noticing the slight shift in Freya’s tone. What was this all about? Why did her mom suddenly have opinions on this?
“Didn’t you propose to Dad first?” Nina asked, assuming Freya simply didn’t agree.
“What if Damian wants to propose to you too?” Freya suggested gently, hoping to talk her out of it. “What if you both end up choosing the same day?”
“Wouldn’t that be romantic?” Nina said dreamily. “Just like what you and Dad…”
Freya was at a loss. How could she convince Nina otherwise?
“Come on, help me out with a few ideas, won’t you?” Nina coaxed, knowing her mom could never say no to her.
“Your dad’s been keeping a close eye on me lately,” Freya said after thinking it over, using Ellis as an excuse with a dead-serious look. “Planning takes time, and he’s not giving me any room.”
“I’ll go talk to him,” Nina offered without missing a beat.
Freya stayed calm. “Alright.”
Nina hadn’t expected her usually supportive mom to play tricks like this. As soon as she went downstairs, Freya quickly sent Ellis a message with the whole conversation.
Ellis texted back, “Now I’m your shield. How do you plan on paying me back?” Freya thought about it for a second and decided not to respond.
Ellis had completely seen her through.
“I’m taking Mom out to run some errands. We’ll be back tomorrow night,” Nina announced, fully aware of how stubborn her dad could be. She didn’t even try to negotiate.
She knew better than anyone—getting her mom away from him was no easy task, especially with how close they were.
“Request denied,” Ellis replied flatly, passing along Freya’s stance.
Nina hadn’t realized she was being played by both her parents. “I’m not asking for permission, I’m telling you what’s happening. And besides, Mom isn’t your property.”
“Our flight’s tomorrow afternoon,” Ellis said without an ounce of sympathy. “There’s an order to things.”
Nina wanted to argue, but she had to admit—it was kind of the family rule.
“Then just tonight,” Nina offered, trying to bargain.
“My wife isn’t up for grabs,” Ellis replied, standing up and tapping her lightly on the forehead. “If you’ve got complaints, take it up with your Damian.”
“I need to talk to Mom about, you know, girl stuff,” Nina pressed, still trying to sway Ellis. All she wanted was a little alone time with her mother. “It’s not the kind of thing I can discuss with Damian.”
“You’ve got Kyra and other female friends,” Ellis offered, knowing full well how close she was with her friends.
“They don’t have any real experience with this kind of thing,” Nina sounded worn out from having to make up excuses. “Only Mom fits the bill.”
“Aren’t you close to Greta and Riley?” Ellis cut right through her act, sticking to the refusal Freya had asked for. “They’re suitable too.”
Nina fell silent, completely speechless. She stared at him. “You just don’t want me to have any alone time with Mom.”
.
.
.
###Chapter 1813
Chapter 1813:
“I thought I’d made that pretty obvious,” Ellis replied smoothly, as if it were the most natural thing in the world.
Nina opened her mouth to argue, but stopped. No matter what she said, her dad would always have something to counter it with.
She felt completely defeated.
Then she blurted, “You two have been together for years. A few days apart isn’t going to kill you. Aren’t you tired of being joined at the hip every single day?”
“As long as I’m with my wife, I’ll never get tired,” Ellis said sincerely.
Nina realized there was no way she’d win this battle and decided to switch gears. “When will you two be back?”
“The week before your official engagement,” Ellis answered plainly.
Nina responded and turned to go upstairs.
Since talking to Freya now was off the table, she decided to bring it up again when the timing felt better.
Over two hours later, Ellis and Freya had just finished bathing. Now they were nestled in bed, warm and relaxed.
Thinking about Nina’s request, Freya turned to Ellis. “Should we just agree to it? If they both propose on the same day, it might actually be quite sweet.” Their daughter had already brought it up. A joint proposal did sound rather romantic.
“No need. Damian can be the one to propose. Nina doesn’t have to,” Ellis replied, wrapping his arms around her.
“If we don’t say yes, she’s just going to keep obsessing over it.” Freya did not want their daughter to stress about it every day.
“She wants to propose just to show Damian how much she loves him.” Ellis understood emotions deeply. He gently rubbed her head to reassure her. “But he already understands how deeply she feels for him. She doesn’t need to prove it.”
Freya stayed quiet, still turning the thought over in her mind.
Ellis leaned in, brushing his lips against hers. “Don’t worry. Everything will fall into place soon.”
Freya blinked, confused. Then something clicked. She narrowed her eyes slightly. “What do you mean by that?”
“While you were chatting with Nina earlier, Damian messaged me. He asked if we’re free the Friday after next!”
Ellis handed over his phone to show her the messages. “That’s when he’s planning to propose.”
Freya scanned the conversation.
Once she’d finished reading, Ellis asked, “Still worried?”
“Not anymore,” Freya said, feeling her heart settle.
There was one week left.
During that time, Nina would probably still be tossing around ideas with her friends about how to plan her own proposal.
As long as she hadn’t started arranging anything, Damian’s proposal would come as a complete surprise.
At that very moment, Nina was up in her room, video-chatting with Damian. Her tone was as lively and animated as always, chatting about anything and everything. Damian, though not naturally talkative, replied to every single thing she said.
.
.
.
###Chapter 1814
Chapter 1814:
“Tomorrow, I’m going to live with Jesse,” Nina shared a bit of her day, relaxed and smiling. “But if he gets a girlfriend before we’re married, can I move in with you?”
For now, she was staying with Jesse just for the company. They shared a villa, and it was pretty comfortable. But if Jesse got into a relationship, she wouldn’t want to be a third wheel.
“As long as you want to, my place is always your home,” Damian replied without hesitation, bold and straight to the point.
Nina lit up with a bright smile. “Then I’ll come see you tomorrow.”
“No,” Damian cut her off instantly.
Nina blinked, momentarily thrown off. His quick rejection caught her off guard. Her brows furrowed slightly. “The way you said that… it sounds like you’re hiding something.”
“I’ve just been really busy lately. I wouldn’t have time to spend with you.” Damian realized his tone had come off too harsh. He added more gently, “Once this busy stretch is over, I’ll come pick you up myself.”
“Really?” Nina asked, trusting him completely.
Damian gave a firm nod.
After kissing him through the screen, Nina told him to get some rest.
The real reason she’d called, aside from missing him, was to see whether the emotions he showed during the day had been real or just for show. Now it seemed like he truly was getting better. That made her happy.
That night, Nina slept soundly. The next morning, after Freya and Ellis had left for the airport, she returned to the place she shared with Jesse.
After parking the car, she punched in the code and pushed the door open.
What she didn’t expect was to see a girl inside the house.
Standing in the doorway, she caught sight of a cool-looking young lady lounging on the couch with a bag of chips in hand, her face unreadable. Nina paused, then cautiously asked, “You are…?”
“Alayna Blake,” the girl replied flatly, offering just her name and nothing else. Nina left the door open behind her and stepped inside. “Did Jesse bring you here?”
“Yeah,” Alayna answered with the same blank expression.
Nina nodded, letting the subject drop for now, though her curiosity had been thoroughly piqued.
She knew Jesse well—he was upright, disciplined. He’d never bring a random woman home. And if it were just a friend or classmate? Still unlikely. This was their shared home.
That could only mean one thing—this woman might actually be Jesse’s girlfriend.
“There are drinks in the fridge and snacks in the cupboard in front of you,” Nina said casually before heading upstairs. “Help yourself to anything.”
Alayna gave a small nod, her tone still flat. “Thanks.”
Nina offered a polite smile, then went to her room.
Without overthinking it, she immediately dialed Jesse. He’d brought someone home without saying a word to her. That was crossing a line.
Just as the call connected, a knock sounded at her door, making her jump. She ended the call and tossed her phone onto the bed, assuming Alayna had come to talk.
But when she opened the door, she blinked, surprised to see him there. Jesse stood before her, dressed in a suit, his handsome features slightly more tense than usual.
“Come to the study with me,” he said.
Nina followed him without question.
As they passed through the hallway, she caught him casting a glance downstairs. So, that woman wasn’t his girlfriend?
When the study door closed behind them, Nina noticed the neat stack of documents on the desk and the open laptop from a recently ended video call.
Clearly, Jesse had been working from home today.
“What’s going on?” Nina asked, unable to contain her curiosity any longer.
.
.
.
